raw.assessment: The incumbent supplies an assembled, rearrangeable organizer and enabled seven of ten observed customers to reach their ordered arrangement unaided (D2-O4). Its 11-minute median and five reported partition problems indicate unresolved performance, although reports do not establish verified omission rates (D2-O2, D2-O3). D2-O6 limits an account in which assembly is uniformly too slow: repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, while every extreme delay occurred in mixed batches. Layout complexity and switching remain confounded. Width overlap in D2-O5 also limits a width-only explanation of insertion retries. No supplied observation establishes the pilot targets or identifies a single dominant cause.

openings.claim: Does changing layout between orders increase selection and checking time independently of compartment count?
openings.delta: Distinguishes a sequencing bottleneck from intrinsically slower complex layouts before changing the assembled product.
openings.prediction: A switching effect predicts longer selection/checking for the same layout immediately after a different layout; a complexity effect predicts longer times by compartment count even in repeated runs.
openings.probe: Using reusable samples within the 15-sample allowance, have both workers perform matched layouts in repeated and interleaved sequences, counterbalancing sequence order and holding exterior color constant. Time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately; record component discrepancies. Limit trials to time compatible with the fixed delivery date.
assumptions: Trial time fits available working time and the initial spending cap.
Practice and fatigue are sufficiently balanced to interpret differences.

openings.claim: An order-specific diagram identifying the short partition and its destination may improve unaided arrangement success.
openings.delta: Targets the observed localization difficulty without removing workshop assembly or partition rearrangeability.
openings.prediction: With independently verified complete kits, the revised diagram produces fewer short-partition placement errors and help requests than the existing three-layout diagram.
openings.probe: Assign the ten willing participants to matched ordered layouts with either diagram; verify contents first and record placement errors, help requests and completion time. Use this small comparison to assess the mechanism, then retain the 60-unit targets for pilot acceptance. Measure diagram preparation time and costs before adoption.
assumptions: Diagram ambiguity contributes to difficulty even when contents are correct.
Revision fits both cost caps and the fixed delivery date while retaining selected compartments, color, footprint and capacity.

raw.assessment: Two unverified counterfactual hypotheses. Combined timings conceal causes; ten participants cannot establish pilot customer success. All footprint, capacity, reversibility, budget, accepted configuration/color, and delivery constraints remain binding.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: forbid full assembly before dispatch; supply the existing base and loose partitions with an order-specific inventory/layout sheet explicitly locating the short partition.
openings.delta: Transfer partition insertion to customers; make the ordered arrangement and component inventory explicit.
openings.prediction: Workshop time falls only if added preparation/checking costs less than insertion. Nine of ten trial users achieve their ordered layout unaided.
openings.probe: Use ten sample sets and ten participants across compartment variants. Time every workshop stage, including sheet preparation; compare matched assembled samples. Record unaided arrangement, assortment fit, completeness, and handling damage. Reject if spending or delivery limits fail; this screen cannot establish pilot rates.
assumptions: Replacement dependencies: accurate order-to-inventory/layout mapping; affordable sheet production; distinguishable parts; customer insertion ability; loose-part retention by existing packaging; predispatch contents verification.
Existing parts preserve capacity and reversible connections; preparation fits spending caps and delivery date.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: forbid shared open shape bins during assembly; one worker prepares complete order sets in reusable board trays, and the other checks, assembles, and packs each set.
openings.delta: Replace simultaneous shared picking with a verified component-set handoff; retain full assembly.
openings.prediction: Mixed-layout picking/correction delays decline, although insertion difficulty may persist. Tray preparation and waiting could erase gains.
openings.probe: Reuse five remaining samples in matched mixed-layout sequences, alternating worker roles. Compare total worker-minutes, per-order elapsed time, errors, preparation, and waiting against shared-bin assembly; include rare colors. Count tray fabrication and setup.
assumptions: Replacement dependencies: reusable trays; accurate component lists and color identifiers; one-bench staging space; replenishment; reliable handoff/checking.
Tray construction and workflow fit both spending caps and the fixed delivery date; existing product geometry and removable connections are retained.

openings.claim: Switching may delay picking/checking independently of complexity.
openings.discriminator: Same-layout switch penalty versus compartment-count effect.
openings.probe: Both workers counterbalance repeats/interleaving; fix color; time stages/errors using reusable samples.

openings.claim: Order-specific short-partition diagrams may improve arrangement.
openings.discriminator: Fewer placement errors/help requests with complete kits.
openings.probe: Ten participants compare diagrams on matched layouts; verify contents; measure completion and preparation costs/time.

openings.claim: Ship loose partitions with inventory/layout sheets; customers perform insertion.
openings.discriminator: Preparation/checking saves insertion time; nine of ten arrange unaided.
openings.probe: Ten sets versus assembled samples: time stages/sheets; check arrangement, completeness, capacity, damage.
openings.uncertainty: Mapping, distinguishability, customer ability, packaging retention required.

openings.claim: Replace shared-bin picking with prepared trays and verified worker handoff.
openings.probe: Five reusable samples; matched mixed sequences, alternate roles, rare colors; measure worker-minutes, elapsed time, errors, setup/waiting.
openings.uncertainty: Space, lists/color identification, replenishment, checking required; insertion difficulty persists.

post_distill.decision: Probe, then decide. All require 30x20 cm, same assortment, removable partitions, initial <=500, added materials <=0.40/order, accepted counts/colors and fixed delivery. Reuse <=15 samples. Reports do not verify omissions; width overlap leaves insertion cause unresolved. Small probes cannot establish pilot targets: >=98% complete, median <=8 minutes, >=90% unaided.
